description: Telraam is a citizen-science traffic counting system: a low-cost sensor placed in a resident's window continuously counts traffic on the street outside by mode, including motor vehicles, heavy vehicles, cyclists and pedestrians. Counts from each device are shared on a public page for the street, showing counts and direction for four categories, night counts, daily and hourly overviews, speed, modal split and rankings for the past two weeks. Device owners get a personal dashboard with raw data export, and premium or network subscriptions add ten vehicle categories, 15-minute data, trends, live traffic, reports and advanced API access. The European Union's WeCount project (2019 to 2021) developed the platform and sensor kits with citizens. Coverage is wherever devices are installed, mainly European towns and cities. Access: basic data free on the public map and with a free subscription, advanced data and API access paid; the terms reserve Telraam's intellectual property rights and no open data licence is named. Caveats: counts come from volunteers' windows, so coverage is patchy and daylight dependent for older sensors. It supports local traffic volume, active mobility and road safety analysis and calibration of urban traffic models, and complements Strava Metro and the Norwegian Trafikkdata counts catalogued here.
